neighbours.label: The word ' of' right after 'several' (strongest) or 'many' in mid-sentence object position (rain ruined several of our photos); quiet for 'some of', 'most of', 'all of', 'a few of', 'each of' and for other uses of 'of' (made of, afraid of, the roof of). Also fires weaker on ' achievement' in 'breadth of achievement'.
fire: The storm last night ruined several of our photos from the trip.
She invited several of her old classmates to the reunion.
We lost many of the seedlings to the early frost.
The coach benched several of the starting players after the loss.
He had read many of the books on the reading list before class began.
The museum lent several of its rarest paintings to the exhibition.
